A surface trough extending between Invest 96W to the east-southeast 
and Tropical Depression 28W to the north-northwest will encroach upon
Saipan and Tinian tonight and linger through Thursday, bringing
scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms. The zones were split 
due to short-term differences in shower coverage as drier air will 
remain over Guam and Rota. Island-effect showers may be possible for
these islands, but easterly winds are expected to advect these 
showers over western coastal waters, similar to the pattern that 
occurred today. Afterwards, isolated showers will return for the 
entire region through Friday night. Then, weather conditions may 
begin to deteriorate Saturday as Invest 96W potentially tracks 
through the Marianas as a tropical storm or typhoon. Widespread 
locally heavy showers, near-gale winds, and thunderstorms are 
forecast from Saturday night through Sunday night, with a peak of the
worst conditions around Sunday. Shortly afterwards, shower coverage 
looks to decrease to isolated with light and variable winds possibly 
returning after Monday night. Residents of the Marianas should 
continue storm preparations and stay up to date with the forecasts in
the coming days.

Marine...
Altimetry data indicates combined seas of 3 to 4 feet. Seas are
expected to increase a foot or two through Friday. Then, seas will
significantly increase sometime Friday night ahead of Invest 96W,
with conditions hazardous to small craft possible through Monday.
Light east winds will become light to moderate northeasterlies by 
late Thursday, before rapidly increasing through the weekend. There
is a moderate risk of rip currents along north and east facing reefs
at least through Thursday night with dangerous surf conditions 
probable this weekend. Those with marine interests should monitor the
forecasts in the coming days.

Hydrology...
Invest 96W continues to develop north of Pohnpei and Kosrae. 
Ensemble model guidance continues to show a passage anywhere between 
Guam to north of Saipan as a tropical storm or typhoon. Uncertainty 
is still high regarding timing, location, and intensity, but the 
potential for locally heavy rainfall and flooding continues to 
increase approaching this weekend. This is expected to produce 5 to 8
inches of rainfall between Saturday and Monday, with localized 
amounts up to 12 inches possible. As showers are likely to persist, 
consistent rainfall is likely to saturate the soils enough to 
increase chance for mudslides. Residents on these islands need to 
closely monitor this developing situation as flood watches, 
advisories, and flash flood warnings could be issued later this 
weekend.

Tropical Systems...
Tropical Depression (TD) 28W is currently located south of Iwo To 
near 21.0N 143.1E, and it is moving northwest at 13 mph. 28W is 
expected to maintain this general course with a slight decrease in 
forward speed through Thursday. Maximum sustained winds are around 30
mph, and it is expected to maintain this intensity through tonight, 
remaining a tropical depression as it weakens slightly through 
Thursday. Satellite reveals a weak low-level circulation center with
isolated thunderstorms along the northern and southeast flanks, with
little convective activity elsewhere. 28W is expected to continue to
weaken through the end of the week as it opens into a surface wave, 
somewhere west of Iwo To.

For more information please refer to bulletins from the Joint
Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN31 PGTW and from the
National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ31 PGUM.

A developing tropical disturbance, Invest 96W, is located to the 
northeast of Pohnpei, near 9.0N 160.4E. As of 5 AM ChST this morning,
Invest 96W remains the subject of a Tropical Cyclone Formation Alert
(TCFA) by the JTWC, which means it is expected to develop into a 
significant tropical cyclone (a tropical depression) within 24 hours.
Himawari visible satellite imagery this afternoon shows a very 
broad, elongated disturbance stretching along roughly 10N, with 
numerous to widespread showers and isolated thunderstorms located 
along its western and southwestern flanks, focused over and south of 
Pohnpei. The low-level circulation center and eastern flank are 
mostly exposed, with patchy showers seen across the area including
the northern Marshall Islands. Lines of thunderstorms are seen along
a convergence boundary within 96W's southwest flank, which extend 
east-southeast from around Chuuk Lagoon to Kosrae. Deterministic and
ensemble model guidance continue to show the development of a broad 
tropical cyclone over the next few days with most tracks depicting a 
Marianas passage sometime between late Saturday evening and Sunday 
night. Although most tracks take the developing cyclone directly 
through the southern Marianas, individual model tracks range from
